tasks.short: Explain communication strategies to patient and family, practise them together, choose take-home information, send it and answer questions between sessions.

steps.what: Speech therapist educates patients and family members about communication techniques
Speech therapist practises the strategies with the family
Speech therapist looks for or writes take-home information for the family
Speech therapist e-mails the handouts to the family
Speech therapist answers families' questions between sessions

tasks.design: A library of handouts and short videos approved by the practice's therapists sits in the patient record ({OTHER}); the therapist ticks the ones that fit, and once chosen they go to the family through the patient portal. Explaining, practising and answering questions stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Handouts were searched for or written per family and printed.
tasks.enabler_now: Record systems hold handout libraries and send them through patient portals.
tasks.still_hard: Families learn strategies by practising, not by reading.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a husband stop finishing his wife's sentences after her stroke.

reach.learn: Whether shared handouts help ward staff.

evidence.claim: Record systems hold libraries of approved handouts and send them through patient portals.
Health data are special category data; information to families goes through a secure channel.

assumptions: Boundary: from therapy goals to questions answered; therapy sessions on other goals are outside.
Input contract: handout library approved by the practice's therapists; fallback is printing.
Explaining, practising and answering do not change.
research_questions: Do families use the handouts at home?

incremental.description: Speech therapist keeps the handout library current.

approvals.approved_version: The handouts chosen by the therapist in s3; other handouts need a new choice before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is in person.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the team's notes, discuss patients in the team meeting, supervise assistants and students, record agreements and tell colleagues about changes.

steps.what: Speech therapist reads notes from the other disciplines before the team meeting
Speech therapist collaborates with the therapy team in the patient meeting
Speech therapist supervises assistants and students in sessions
Speech therapist writes the team agreements in the record
Speech therapist messages colleagues about changes in a patient's care

tasks.design: A team view in the patient record ({OTHER}) shows each discipline's current goals and latest note on one screen, so less searching is needed before the meeting. Agreements are entered per goal in a short form during the meeting, and changes reach colleagues as tasks in the record instead of separate messages. Meetings and supervision stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were spread across tabs and agreements written up after the meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: Record systems offer team views and task lists.
tasks.still_hard: Good teamwork comes from talking, not screens.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a student is losing confidence and stepping in gently.

reach.learn: Whether a team view shortens team meetings.

evidence.claim: Record systems offer team views per patient and task lists for colleagues.
The dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from reading notes to colleagues informed; treatment sessions are outside.
Input contract: notes and goals written by each discipline in the record; fallback is reading every tab.
Meetings and supervision do not change.
Colleagues' time is outside the therapist's savings.
research_questions: Are agreements followed up more often?

incremental.description: Speech therapist keeps goals current in the team view.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is meetings and supervision.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather test scores and session notes, write the progress report, send it to parents and school, take part in the progress meeting and record the agreed actions.

steps.what: Speech therapist gathers test scores and session notes for the report
Speech therapist writes reports for meetings regarding patients' progress

loop.input: Session notes since the last report, test scores and the therapy goals.
loop.output: A draft progress section per goal, each statement linked to a dated note.
loop.check: Code copies scores from the record and flags statements without a linked note; the therapist edits and approves every section.
loop.stop: One draft per report; nothing is sent without approval.
loop.why_not_simpler: Progress is described in free-text notes that a template cannot summarise.

steps.what: Speech therapist e-mails the report to parents and the school
Speech therapist participates in the progress meeting with school, parents and team
Speech therapist writes up the agreed actions after the meeting

tasks.design: The report template in the patient record ({OTHER}) pulls in test scores and goals. A bounded step drafts the progress section per goal from the session notes, linking each statement to a dated note, and the therapist edits and approves every section; only then does it go to parents and, with their consent, the school. Taking part in the meeting stays with the therapist, and agreed actions go into a short form.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scores and notes were copied by hand and reports written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models can draft summaries from notes, and record systems fill templates.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can overstate progress; the therapist must check each statement.
tasks.human_edge: Telling parents honestly that progress has stalled.
tasks.altitude: The therapist edits a drafted report instead of writing it.

evidence.claim: In a study of 236,153 scribe notes, clinicians' self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes (three of seven authors from the vendor).
Providers are legally responsible for careful use of generative AI: assess risks, train, test and monitor.
Sharing a child's health information with the school needs the parents' consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the record to the action record; carrying out the actions is outside.
Input contract: notes and scores in the patient record; parents' consent recorded before sharing; fallback is writing by hand.
Parents' and school staff's time is outside the therapist's savings.
research_questions: How much of the drafted text does the therapist keep?

already_counted.description: Speech therapist edits the drafted report.

incremental.description: Speech therapist audits a sample of drafts each month.

approvals.approved_version: The report as approved by the therapist in s2; changes need a new approval before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The meeting itself stays the same.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Demonstrate and practise oral-motor and breathing exercises, correct the client's movements, choose home exercises, send them and note progress.

steps.what: Speech therapist teaches clients to strengthen tongue, jaw and face muscles and control breathing
Speech therapist watches and corrects the client's movements
Speech therapist prepares home exercise sheets
Speech therapist hands the printed exercise sheets to the client
Speech therapist notes the exercises done and progress

tasks.design: An exercise library with short videos in the practice's home-exercise app ({OTHER}) lets the therapist pick exercises, repetitions and frequency; once the programme is set, the app sends it to the client's phone. Exercises are ticked in the session note from the same list. Teaching and correcting stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exercise sheets were written or copied and handed out on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Home-exercise apps hold video libraries and send programmes to clients.
tasks.still_hard: Clients who do exercises wrongly at home need correction in the next session.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling through touch whether the jaw is relaxed.

reach.learn: Whether one exercise app serves both disciplines.

evidence.claim: Home-exercise apps hold video libraries and send exercise programmes to clients.
Health data are special category data; the app needs a processor agreement.

assumptions: Boundary: from therapy goals to the session note; assessment is outside.
Input contract: exercise videos approved by the practice's therapists; fallback is paper sheets.
Teaching and correcting do not change.
Clients without a smartphone get printed sheets.
research_questions: Do clients do their home exercises more often?

incremental.description: Speech therapist prints sheets for clients without a smartphone.

approvals.approved_version: The programme set by the therapist in s3; changed exercises need a new setting before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is hands-on teaching.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The speech therapist keeps teaching, practising, teamwork and progress talks; handouts, copying scores and writing reports from scratch shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A therapist who spends saved time on longer practice with clients.
